critical_code_review_comments: getBuyerBudget() fix is correct and minimal — uses prisma.buyer.findFirst({ where: { user: { supabaseId: user.id } } }) which correctly traverses the User→Buyer relation via Supabase auth UUID. Pattern matches /app/frontend/lib/auth/api.ts.

DELETE /api/buyer/shortlist handler correctly scopes deleteMany by both shortlistId and inventoryItemId, preventing cross-buyer deletion. Returns {removed:count} which is honest about whether anything was removed.

AddToShortlistButton's ALREADY_IN_SHORTLIST → done=true UX choice intentionally hides the duplicate-add as success. This matches spec but might confuse a buyer who expects 'already added' feedback. Consider a distinct 'Already in your shortlist' label rather than reusing the 'Added' success state. (Optional polish — spec accepts this behavior.)

Anonymous and 'authed-but-no-prequal' both render the same /auth/signup CTA. Iter25 review already flagged this — the fix masks the fact that 'no prequal' state is indistinguishable from anon. Not a regression, but worth a follow-up branch for buyers who signed up but haven't prequal'd.

rca of the issue: ROOT CAUSE: page.tsx getBuyerBudget() previously used `prisma.buyer.findUnique({ where: { userId: user.id } })`, but user.id from supabase.auth.getUser() is the Supabase auth UUID, not the local Prisma User.id. Buyer.userId is a FK to the local User row. The lookup always returned null, so buyerBudget was null, so the page rendered the anon /auth/signup CTA branch even for fully-authenticated buyers with prequal. FIX: switched to `prisma.buyer.findFirst({ where: { user: { supabaseId: user.id } } })` which traverses the relation correctly. CONFIRMED RESOLVED: authed buyer now sees <BUTTON>Add to Shortlist with 'Within your pre-qualified budget' badge.
